lineage.upstreamOperation: Concrete hybrid KEM vectors from the CFRG reference implementation: seed → keys, randomness → ciphertext and shared secret
lineage.localOperation: Through the hub's PKCS#11 binding on the SoftHSM3 Rust engine (src/wasm/hpkePqVectors.local.test.ts): seed imported as CKA_SEED on CKM_HPKE_KEM_KEY_PAIR_GEN, public key compared with encapsulation_key; C_EncapsulateKey(CKM_HPKE, HKDF-SHA256/AES-256-GCM) with the test-only forced randomness compared with ciphertext; the recipient's C_DecapsulateKey derives the same base nonce and AEAD key (seal/open round trip). The shared secret itself is checked by the engine's cargo tests (rust/src/hpke_pq_vectors_tests.rs).

transformations.detail: The hub replay compares encapsulation_key (from the imported seed) and ciphertext (from the forced randomness) through the PKCS#11 binding and checks that both sides derive the same AEAD key; decapsulation_key, decapsulation_key_pq, decapsulation_key_t and shared_secret are not compared there (CKM_HPKE never releases them) and are checked by the engine's cargo tests instead.

files.notes: Added 2026-10-01 with pqctoday-hsm #310 (seed-format hybrid HPKE keys, forced encapsulation randomness for KATs). QUARANTINED pending the WS-I two-person vector-source review. Internet-Draft: a claim must name the draft, never call it a standard.

verification.method: Re-fetched the upstream file at the pinned commit: its SHA-256 equals the recorded upstreamSha256, and every field of every local case equals the upstream case with the same tcId after the renames/normalizations recorded in lineage.

Not used: CMAC-TDES and HMAC-SHA2-512/224, /256 (not in PKCS#11 v3.2 Table 196), bit-oriented output lengths, the remaining groups.

Only the `invalid` cases are vendored (see excluded_cases): each carries an ek that must be refused (FIPS 203 §7.2 modulus check, or a wrong length), at C_CreateObject or at C_EncapsulateKey.

transformations.detail: ONE top-level `_provenance` key added (attribution, pinned commit, upstream path + sha256, Apache-2.0 licence, evidence class, result policy and the excluded_cases list). Every kept case is the pinned upstream case byte-for-byte: no tcId renumbered, no value re-derived or normalized.

133 upstream case(s) dropped by a DECLARED rule (encaps-valid), listed by tgId/tcId in the file's _provenance.excluded_cases: C_EncapsulateKey (PKCS#11 v3.2 §5.18.8) takes no caller-supplied randomness: the token draws m itself, so (ek, m) -> (c, K) cannot be reproduced and the upstream c/K cannot be byte-compared. The same limit already makes NIST's encapsulation AFT groups a declared skip (mlkem_encapdecap_val_test notExecuted). The `invalid` cases need no m — their ek must be refused — so they are vendored and executed. `vendor_wycheproof.py --check` re-applies the rule to the pinned upstream file and fails unless exactly those cases are dropped and every other case is kept unchanged.

transformations.detail: ONE top-level `_provenance` key added (attribution, pinned commit, upstream path + sha256, Apache-2.0 licence, evidence class, result policy and the excluded_cases list). 133 upstream case(s) dropped by a DECLARED rule (encaps-valid), listed by tgId/tcId in the file's _provenance.excluded_cases: C_EncapsulateKey (PKCS#11 v3.2 §5.18.8) takes no caller-supplied randomness: the token draws m itself, so (ek, m) -> (c, K) cannot be reproduced and the upstream c/K cannot be byte-compared. The same limit already makes NIST's encapsulation AFT groups a declared skip (mlkem_encapdecap_val_test notExecuted). The `invalid` cases need no m — their ek must be refused — so they are vendored and executed. `vendor_wycheproof.py --check` re-applies the rule to the pinned upstream file and fails unless exactly those cases are dropped and every other case is kept unchanged.

lineage.localOperation: C_GenerateKeyPair(CKM_ML_DSA_KEY_PAIR_GEN, CKA_SEED = privateSeed in the private template); the generated public CKA_VALUE is byte-compared with publicKey; then deterministic C_Sign as in the noseed file, byte-compared with sig. privateKeyPkcs8 is not used (transport encoding). An `invalid` case (seed of the wrong length, ctx > 255 bytes) must be refused.

transformations.detail: ONE top-level `_provenance` key added (attribution, pinned commit, upstream path + sha256, Apache-2.0 licence, evidence class, result policy and the excluded_cases list). Every kept case is the pinned upstream case byte-for-byte: no tcId renumbered, no value re-derived or normalized.

1 upstream case(s) dropped by a DECLARED rule (sign-randomized), listed by tgId/tcId in the file's _provenance.excluded_cases: CK_SIGN_ADDITIONAL_CONTEXT (PKCS#11 v3.2) carries hedgeVariant and context only; there is no parameter for an explicit rnd, so a hedged signature made with the upstream rnd cannot be reproduced. Same limit as NIST's hedged sigGen groups (declaredUnreachable mldsa-hedged-rnd). `vendor_wycheproof.py --check` re-applies the rule to the pinned upstream file and fails unless exactly those cases are dropped and every other case is kept unchanged.

files.notes: Scope rule WYC-SCOPE-1 (scripts/acvp/vendor_wycheproof.py): vendored because src/components/Playground/hsm/acvp/sections/wycheproofPqc.ts executes every vendored case of this file against both engines. 1 upstream case(s) are NOT vendored, by the declared rule recorded in lineage (type subset) and in the file's _provenance.excluded_cases. 4 case(s) are Wycheproof `invalid`: reject-path evidence NIST does not publish.
